segments.title: The hold
sentences: This page is loud. Not with sound, but with other people's urgency.
Eight notifications drift around a grainy orb, each one asking for a piece of you.
There is one control. A key, held for twelve seconds.
This is Hush, and the whole product is the hold.
segments.notes: Cold open on the real page. One control, one gesture, twelve seconds. Name the product by the fourth line.

segments.title: The noise
sentences: Each notification is a chip with its own orbit, its own speed, its own drift.
None of them line up. A feed is not a list, it is a field of small pulls.
The orb in the middle is noise too: a texture of random grey, going nowhere.
segments.notes: Eight real chips on their real orbits. The noise orb is the actual 256px texture, clipped to a circle.

segments.title: One gesture
sentences: The gesture is a press and hold.
Space on the keyboard, or the keycap itself. The page listens for both.
The moment you press down, it starts counting. The moment you let go, it stops.
segments.notes: The keycap, drawn at scale. Two input paths converge on beginHold. The state machine stays idle until the press.

segments.title: The pull
sentences: Focus is a number here, and it climbs from zero to one over twelve seconds.
Each chip has its own delay, so the pull arrives in waves.
As the number rises, every orbit tightens and every chip shrinks.
The noise is not deleted. It is drawn inward.
segments.notes: The real formula: local = (p - delay) / (1 - delay), pull = smoothstep(local), orbit += pull * 3.4, scale = 1 - pull * 0.88.

segments.title: It comes back
sentences: At the end of the spiral, a chip crosses a threshold and is absorbed.
It leaves a burst of particles and a chime, panned to the side it came from.
A second later, a new chip arrives.
The noise always comes back. That is the honest part.
segments.notes: One chip's lifecycle on a loop. 14 particles per absorption, five chime notes, pan from -0.7 to 0.7, respawn in 1.2 to 2.8s.

segments.title: The static
sentences: Look at the orb.
It is a two hundred and fifty six pixel square of random grey, drawn inside a circle.
As focus rises, the noise falls from thirty two percent opacity to about five.
Underneath it, a mint glow fades in.
segments.notes: Square noise texture, circular clip, drift offset. Alpha 0.32 * (1 - 0.85f) goes from 0.32 to 0.048. Split orb at f=0 and f=1.

segments.title: The clock
sentences: The ring is the clock.
It fills once over twelve seconds, with a bright tip at the exact moment.
The copy changes with it: stay with it, almost quiet, don't let go.
One variable drives the ring, the words and the readout below.
segments.notes: Big ring, filling. Three copy bands at 0.34 and 0.70. Readout counts 0.0 to 12.0.

segments.title: The leak
sentences: Now let go early.
The progress does not pause. It drains about ten times faster than it filled.
Twelve seconds to reach the quiet. About one and a fifth to lose it.
Focus is not a state you enter. It is something you keep choosing.
segments.notes: The thesis. Fill slope 1/12 per second, drain 0.85 per second. 12.0s up, 1.18s down. Plot both over 26 seconds.

segments.title: The quiet
sentences: Hold to the end, and the page blooms.
A hundred and twenty particles, a four note chord, and one line: it's quiet now.
The small urgencies are gone.
With reduced motion, the particles stop and the bloom simplifies. The quiet still arrives.
segments.notes: The payoff frame. Bloom particles, A major chord A3 C#4 E4 A4, reduced-motion variant beside it.

segments.title: One page
sentences: Hush is one page of TypeScript, Canvas and Web Audio.
The orb is drawn, the chips are DOM elements, the sound is synthesized on the spot.
No images, no audio files, no backend.
Hold the key. That is the whole product.
segments.notes: Three files, three layers. Close on the keycap and the smallest true sentence in the film.
